To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) receiver sensitivity is the dominant factor in determining link power efficiency, (ii) a physics-based design methodology is required to optimize link performance, and (iii) heterogenous-integrated opto-electronic platforms can achieve state-of-the-art link power consumption and performance.

the front-end receiver design has a significant impact on link power efficiency, which is the most important metric for future optical communication system design, and that the front-end design is the most important parameter to optimize for future system efficiency.

1) the photo-receiver is the most important component in controlling link power, 2) heterogeneously integrated photonic+CMOs platforms offer the best link performance and 3) the link performance is ultimately limited by the speed of the digital sampler, which can be improved through advanced CMOS technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of opto-electronics communication links, and the development of a physical model for the link design process.
the design, analysis, and optimization of opto-electric communication links.
the design and optimization of opto-electric communication links.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first time a first principles approach has been applied to the design of opto-electronics communication links.
the first principles, physical design approach presented here is an essential step towards realizing low-power, high-speed, high-performance opto-electronic systems.
this work represents a first principles, holistic, and end-to-end optimization of opto-electric communication links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first principles, end to end analysis of opto electronic communication links which incorporates the receiver circuit optimization.
the first principles approach is a powerful tool for optimizing opto-electronic links, and it can be applied to any platform.

we are able to show that the receiver is the most power-hungry component of an opto-electronic link, and that the receiver sensitivity and the power budget are the most important metrics for the overall link efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a first principles approach to link optimization can greatly accelerate the design process and provide valuable insights for system-level optimization.
a holistic approach to system optimization is necessary to achieve state-of-the-art system performance.
the link performance is determined by the receiver circuitry and not the laser transmitter.
